title: Change-feed consumption — Incremental Index Updater (Signature)
description:
Signature edition — an original Signature-authored completion, clearly labeled as Signature work and never presented as public record. The incremental index updater keeps indexes fresh between full rebuilds by applying only what changed: new records, modified records, deletions. It consumes a change feed, batches updates for efficiency, and maintains the auxiliary structures (deletion bitmaps, version maps) that let a mutable index stay correct. Done well, the archive is searchable seconds after ingestion instead of hours after the next rebuild.

This record documents the change-feed consumption approach: Tail the source's change log (inserts, updates, deletes) as the single input to updates.

Teaching ladder rank 1 (foundations): this record explains the core idea in plain terms — what inputs the tool takes, what outputs it produces, and when it is the right choice for an archive task.

Every record in this database is the full fully-formed file with all data — never a stub or description alone. This database holds 15 of the 1,000,000 target — the march to a million is in progress.
demo:
# Incremental Index Updater demo: change feed -> upserts, deletes, version guard.
index={}; versions={}
def apply(change):
    rid=change["id"]
    if change["op"]=="delete":
        index.pop(rid,None); versions[rid]=change["v"]; return "deleted "+rid
    if versions.get(rid,0)>change["v"]: return "skipped stale "+rid
    index[rid]=change["doc"]; versions[rid]=change["v"]; return "upserted "+rid
feed=[{"op":"upsert","id":"r1","v":1,"doc":"sails"},
      {"op":"upsert","id":"r1","v":1,"doc":"sails"},   # duplicate -> idempotent
      {"op":"upsert","id":"r1","v":0,"doc":"stale"},   # stale -> skipped
      {"op":"delete","id":"r1","v":2}]
for c in feed: print(apply(c))
print("final index:",index)
